Animal Park · ALF-011 (English)

English · Grade 1 · letters and sounds (phonics) · about 12 to 15 minutes

Goal

Recognize the letters E and A by their shape, name and sound, and use them to complete the names of animals and everyday words in English.

What the child does

  • Mission 1 · The letter E: hears that E can say “eh” (hen) and that two E’s together say “ee” (bee), traces the E in stroke order, and taps every E among look-alike letters (F, B, L, H, T).
  • Mission 2 · The letter A: traces the A and taps every A among look-alike letters (V, H, N, M, R).
  • Mission 3 · The missing letter: listens to the word (and, if needed, slowly) and taps the missing letter, E or A: HEN, HAT, RABBIT, BEE, WHALE, SHEEP, STAR, ELEPHANT.
  • Final mission · E and A together: completes words with two or three missing letters: ZEBRA, BEE, ALLIGATOR, SHEEP, ELEPHANT.

Words in the game

  • E: elephant, hen, bee, sheep, zebra.
  • A: alligator, rabbit, hat, whale, star.

Lesson idea (50 min)

  • Circle time (10 min): say the animal names together; children raise a hand when they hear the E sound (“eh”, as in hen) or the A sound (as in hat). Write the words on the board and circle the letters.
  • Game (15 min): in pairs at the table or on a tablet. One child taps, the other says the animal’s name out loud before the answer.
  • Off-screen activity (15 min): “park signs”: cards with animal names missing the E and the A; the children glue cut-out letters in the right place and read the sign to a friend.
  • Wrap-up (10 min): spell three words together (HEN, HAT, BEE) and talk about what was hardest.

Things to watch

  • Does the child mix up E and A only by shape (tracing), or also by sound?
  • In English, a letter’s name and its sound are often different: A is called “ay”, but in hat it says the short A sound; E is called “ee”, but in hen it says “eh”. In WHALE the A says its name and the E at the end is silent; at the end of ZEBRA the A sounds like “uh”. It is worth talking about this with the class.
  • The 🔊 slowly button says the word slowly; the little hand shows the answer after two mistakes on the same letter.
  • The BNCC only brings English from Year 6 on; this version is meant for English lessons in the early years (bilingual or extended programs).
